_comment_AllowedHosts: '*' is fine for local dev (F-13). Production deployments MUST override this with the real public hostname(s) via the AllowedHosts env var or appsettings.Production.json (e.g. 'api.agriforecast.lk') to enable Host-header filtering.

RateLimiting._comment: Request rate limits (security fix F-08). Applied per client IP. These defaults are used when this section is absent — limiting is always ON (fail-closed). 'Global' guards the whole API; 'Auth' is a stricter policy on /api/auth login+register.

Cors._comment: Browser origins allowed to call this API (security fix F-07). Intentionally empty here — no cross-origin access by default. Add dev origins in appsettings.Development.json and production origins via env vars (Cors__AllowedOrigins__0 etc.).

ForwardedHeaders._comment: Trusted reverse-proxy IPs for X-Forwarded-For handling (F-08 rate-limiter partition key). Intentionally EMPTY here — forwarded headers are OFF by default (direct-connection behaviour). PRODUCTION BEHIND A PROXY/LB MUST list the proxy IP(s) here (or via ForwardedHeaders__KnownProxies__0 etc.), otherwise Connection.RemoteIpAddress is the proxy's IP and the rate limiter collapses every client into ONE shared bucket (self-DoS). Only the listed IPs are trusted to set X-Forwarded-For; framework KnownNetworks/KnownProxies defaults are cleared to prevent spoofing.

ConnectionStrings._comment: DefaultConnection is intentionally empty here. Supply it via .NET user-secrets for local dev (dotnet user-secrets set 'ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection' ...) or the ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection environment variable in prod. See appsettings.example.json. NOTE (F-11): TrustServerCertificate=True is acceptable only for local Docker SQL; production connection strings MUST NOT use it — use a real/valid server certificate with Encrypt=True instead.

Jwt._comment: Key is intentionally EMPTY here (security fix F-12). The app fails at startup if Jwt:Key is missing, empty, the old dev placeholder, or < 32 bytes. Supply a strong key via .NET user-secrets for local dev (dotnet user-secrets set 'Jwt:Key' '<value>') or the Jwt__Key environment variable in prod. Must be >= 32 bytes for HS256. See appsettings.Development.example.json.
Jwt._comment_Refresh: RefreshTokenDays sets the stateless refresh-cookie lifetime (default 7). RefreshAudience is optional; when empty it derives to '{Audience}.refresh' so the refresh token is always rejected by the access-token Bearer pipeline.

_comment_MarketPriceSources: Mirrors AgriForecast.Ingestion/appsettings.json. The API now runs ingestion passes itself via POST /api/admin/ingestion/service/start, so it needs the same source settings as the Worker; both hosts fail loudly at startup when a structural key is missing (IngestionPassConfiguration). Keep the two files in step — a divergence means the admin button and the 21:00 job ingest differently.

Cbsl._comment: CBSL Daily Price Report source — LIVE, capture-only. Enabled=true runs the daily incremental pass. Enabled=false is the pause switch: Disabled watermark, a documented no-op, never a source failure.

MlService._comment_harti: HartiLookbackDays: the resume lower bound is (LastObservedDate - HartiLookbackDays) so a bulletin published late for an already-passed date is re-scanned rather than skipped forever. Default 7.
MlService._comment: AdminApiKey is intentionally empty here. It authenticates the /admin/ingest-news, /admin/ingest-harti, /admin/ingest-cbsl and /admin/ingest-cbsl-macro calls to the ML service (X-API-Key header, security fix F-02) and must equal the ML service's ML_ADMIN_API_KEY env var. Supply it via .NET user-secrets for local dev (dotnet user-secrets set 'MlService:AdminApiKey' ...) or the MlService__AdminApiKey environment variable in prod. NOT checked at startup on purpose: it is a secret, and refusing to boot every farmer-facing endpoint over an admin-only feature would be worse than the failure it prevents — a missing key surfaces as a Failed run row naming it.

_comment_WeatherSource: StartDate MUST match AgriForecast.Ingestion/appsettings.json (2025-02-01). It is the lower bound of the weather backfill, so a divergence means an admin-started pass and the 21:00 job ingest different history windows for the same source.

Ingestion._comment: Consumed by the admin ingestion status endpoint (GET /api/admin/ingestion/status). ServiceAddress is echoed to the admin UI as the identity of the process that runs ingestion (the Ingestion Worker, a separate project); it is a label only, no secret. Hosted deployments override it via the Ingestion__ServiceAddress env var. RunningStalenessMinutes is the window past which an unfinished run is treated as crashed (state=stopped) rather than 'running' (default 120).

PipelineSchedule._comment: Consumed by GET /api/admin/pipeline/health to work out which night it should be reporting on. These values MIRROR k8s/pipeline-daily.yaml (schedule '0 21 * * *', timeZone 'Asia/Colombo', startingDeadlineSeconds 21600) and must be changed together with it, or the banner will look for a run in the wrong window. LocalFireTime is HH:mm wall clock in TimeZone. CatchUpWindowMinutes is startingDeadlineSeconds/60: how late a start still counts as that night's run. The 'running' staleness window is shared with Ingestion:RunningStalenessMinutes above. An unresolvable TimeZone falls back to a fixed +05:30 rather than failing the endpoint.

Sentinel._comment: Nightly pipeline email sentinel (PipelineSentinelHostedService). Once a night at LocalCheckTime — wall clock in PipelineSchedule:TimeZone, default 22:30, i.e. 90 minutes after the 21:00 fire — the API reads its own pipeline-health query in-process and emails the owner when the night was NOT green. A night still 'running' is re-read every RunningRecheckMinutes until it reaches a terminal state or until one interval before the next fire. SendGreenHeartbeat=true also sends a short all-clear on a good night; that is deliberate, because an alert-only sentinel is indistinguishable from a broken one — leave it on until the reassurance stops being worth the mail. AdminLogsUrl is the deep link put at the bottom of every message. The sentinel needs the Smtp section below; without it, it logs one line at startup and idles.

Smtp._comment: Outbound mail for the pipeline sentinel — the ONLY thing in this app that sends email. User/From/To/Password are intentionally EMPTY here: no credential and no personal address may be committed. Supply them via .NET user-secrets for local dev (dotnet user-secrets set 'Smtp:User' ...) or the Smtp__User / Smtp__From / Smtp__To / Smtp__Password environment variables in prod (k8s: the optional agri-smtp secret created by k8s/create-secrets.sh). From defaults to User when blank; To accepts a comma-separated list. Gmail needs 2-Step Verification and an APP PASSWORD, not the account password (myaccount.google.com -> Security -> 2-Step Verification -> App passwords). NOT checked at startup on purpose: an unconfigured mailbox must never stop the farmer-facing API from booting — the sentinel just logs 'disabled' and idles.
